title: UK MP Tanmanjeet Singh Dhesi Pushes for NRI Reforms and Direct Flights in Punjab Visit
excerpt: The three-time Slough MP and UK Defence Committee chair met Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann to discuss aviation connectivity, NRI property disputes, extortion threats, and the Kartarpur Corridor.
body:
• UK Labour MP Tanmanjeet Singh Dhesi, who chairs the UK Parliament's Defence Committee, held meetings with Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and NRI Affairs Minister Ravjot Singh during a multi-day visit to the state
  • Dhesi pushed for direct international flights from Amritsar and Chandigarh to the UK and other destinations, a one-window system for resolving NRI property disputes, and reopening of the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor
  • The three-time Slough MP called for coordinated action between India, the UK, Canada, the US, and Australia to combat extortion targeting diaspora business leaders and sports promoters
  • Dhesi donated Rs 2.5 crore for development projects in his native village of Raipur Farala in Punjab's Jalandhar district

UK Member of Parliament Tanmanjeet Singh Dhesi wrapped up a high-profile visit to Punjab this month, holding a series of meetings with the state's top leadership on issues ranging from NRI property disputes and international air connectivity to cross-border security cooperation and the reopening of the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor.

Dhesi, who represents Slough in the UK Parliament and chairs the Defence Committee, met Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann at the Legislative Assembly complex in Chandigarh on August 12. He also held discussions with NRI Affairs Minister Ravjot Singh, Assembly Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan, and Health Minister Balbir Singh.

"I also had the opportunity to raise various issues concerning NRIs with the ministers. Specifically, regarding direct flights from Amritsar and Chandigarh to the UK and other countries worldwide. I believe this will boost trade, business, and tourism here."

— Tanmanjeet Singh Dhesi, UK MP for Slough

Aviation and Connectivity

At the center of Dhesi's agenda was a push to transform Punjab's two international airports — Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport in Amritsar and Shaheed Bhagat Singh International Airport in Chandigarh — into major aviation hubs for North India.

He called for substantially more direct flights connecting both airports to London, Birmingham, and other international destinations, arguing that improved connectivity would reduce the burden on elderly travelers and families who currently face long layovers through Delhi or Gulf hubs. He also stressed the potential for enhanced cargo and commercial air services to boost Punjab's trade and export capacity.

NRI Property Disputes and the One-Window System

Land and property disputes remain one of the most persistent grievances for the Punjabi diaspora. Dhesi raised the issue directly with Chief Minister Mann, emphasizing the need for a mechanism to resolve such cases within a fixed timeframe so that NRIs do not have to make repeated trips to Punjab or endure prolonged litigation.

The proposed one-window system under Punjab's NRI Affairs Department would provide a centralized desk where overseas Punjabis could file complaints, receive case numbers, and track progress digitally. The approach aims to address longstanding complaints about unanswered correspondence, lost files, and stalled hearings that have eroded diaspora confidence in investing back home.

Security and Extortion Concerns

Dhesi pointed to a growing pattern of extortion threats targeting business leaders and sports promoters with ties to Punjab. He called for coordinated efforts between the governments of India, the UK, Canada, Australia, and the United States to address transnational criminal activities affecting the diaspora.

"We also discussed the era of extortion we are currently facing, emphasising the need for strict action. There needs to be coordination between the Government of India and the governments of the UK, Canada, the USA, and Australia, as many people are facing difficulties," Dhesi told reporters in Amritsar.

Kartarpur Corridor and Regional Peace

The UK MP also raised the issue of reopening the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor, the cross-border religious passage connecting India and Pakistan that has been suspended since May 7, 2025, following the Pahalgam terror attack. Dhesi discussed the matter with Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee president Harjinder Singh Dhami, urging that the corridor be reopened to allow devotees to visit the historic gurdwara.

Giving Back to Punjab

Beyond policy discussions, Dhesi made a personal commitment to his home state. The North American Punjabi Association highlighted that the three-time MP donated Rs 2.5 crore for development works in his native village of Raipur Farala in the Jalandhar Cantonment constituency. NAPA Executive Director Satnam Singh Chahal praised the contribution, urging other NRI political leaders to follow Dhesi's example.

"Those NRIs who have achieved success abroad and have entered politics have a special responsibility towards the communities from which they originated," Chahal said. "Their success should also become an opportunity for development back home."

Dhesi was accompanied during his meetings by Parmjeet Singh Raipur, a member of the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee and an Aam Aadmi Party leader.
